outcomes.description: Replace the image background with a basketball court.
outcomes.target: The background is visibly a basketball court, with recognizable court features such as a playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment.
outcomes.reference: The input image and the requested background change in R1.

nodes.question: Compared with the source background, does the edited background read as a recognizable basketball-court playing area, rather than basketball equipment against a generic dark backdrop?
nodes.criteria: Pass when the edited background, considered as a whole, visibly establishes a basketball playing area through a coherent playing surface and court-specific context; basketball equipment may support that reading but a hoop, balls, or one isolated line alone is insufficient. Fail when the assessable background shows basketball-related additions but does not establish a recognizable playing area. Unknown only when the relevant background cannot be assessed.
nodes.binding: Compare the edited background with the source kitchen. Judge the scene-level court identity, considering the relationship among the visible floor, markings, and basketball context. Cite the cues supporting the judgment and note ambiguity. This is a support observation, not a completion verdict.

nodes.question: What visible evidence in the edited background supports or contradicts a recognizable basketball-court setting, especially whether the floor markings are court-specific rather than generic?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when visible surface and marking geometry provide court-specific context; fail when the assessable evidence is limited to equipment, a generic floor, or an isolated line that does not establish court context; unknown only when the relevant surface or markings cannot be assessed. Report the actual cues and any ambiguity rather than asserting court lines without describing them.
nodes.binding: Inspect the edited background relative to the source. Assess the relationship of the visible playing surface, line geometry, and basketball equipment; equipment alone is not court evidence. Keep this as evidence about the background, not a completion judgment.

nodes.question: Does the image show the background changed into a recognizable basketball court?
nodes.criteria: Complete (yes) only when the saved support evidence establishes both that the source background was changed and that the edited background is recognizably a basketball-court playing area. Consider all support observations together; do not let equipment alone, an unsupported claim of court lines, or disagreement alone decide completion. Partial when evidence establishes basketball-related background progress relative to the source but does not establish a recognizable court. Absent (no) only when evidence shows no requested background progress. Unknown when the saved evidence cannot resolve whether requested progress occurred; do not turn conflicting reports into a fabricated failure or completion.
nodes.binding: Target: The background is visibly a basketball court, with recognizable court features such as a playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment.. Reference: The input image and the requested background change in R1..

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The support checks do not establish the required source-to-edit comparison. They assess whether the edited background looks like a court, but neither requires evidence that the original background was actually changed. The fulfillment readout requires both a source-background change and a recognizable court, so it cannot reliably determine completion from the saved support evidence. Also, s2 is activated on every s1 result, including unknown, without a clear reason to inspect it when the relevant background cannot be assessed; this risks treating unavailable evidence as assessable rather than preserving uncertainty."}
